articleHeadline: Document Analysis Reveals Outbreak Response Gaps Across Conflict-Affected
articleSummary: Comparative document analysis evaluates outbreak response policy architecture for conflict settings, using 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo. Outbreak was declared a PHEIC on 17 May 2026. Researchers find standing policy instruments rarely assign operational responsibility for conflict outbreak management; provisions are mostly in operational or humanitarian guidance and time-limited plans, not in continental or national health security instruments. Across the analyzed instruments, deficits are pronounced: only a minority receive strong ratings, and a substantial share is entirely absent. Strong ratings are higher in operational guidance and Bundibugyo-specific instruments, but minimal across standing laws, policies, and national plans. Four IHR (2005) monitoring reports contain no strong ratings. Gaps include surveillance for forcibly displaced populations and areas outside state control, and absence of assigned accountability for surveillance and specialized interventions. The study advocates Africa Health Security and Sovereignty Agenda and revisions to IHR/national plans to establish permanent ownership of safeguards.
notes: 記事は2026年Bundibugyoエボラ流行（既にPHEIC宣言済み）に関する既存の対応政策の文書分析研究であり、新規アウトブレイク情報ではないため新規シグナルとしての価値は低い。ただし当該エボラ流行自体の最新状況については別途モニタリングが望ましい。

articleSummary: Six months after the May 15 declaration of the 17th Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the response shows scientific and logistical gains but is constrained by structural obstacles. The outbreak echoes the 2018–2020 crisis and underscores enduring zoonotic risks and the need for sustained health-system investment.

To mitigate, use disposable nonwoven slippers or bring your own; if using public slippers, rinse and wash feet promptly after wearing. Public wet floors in hotel showers, pools, or gym areas sustain fungi and skin infections; HPV strains 1–4 can cause plantar warts in moist, warm conditions. Hand dryers in public toilets may disperse bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella, Staphylococcus aureus) and fail to sterilize them; wipe hands with paper towels or air-dry away from dryers. Practical tips: avoid direct contact with public items; don’t go barefoot with foot injuries; and refuse hand-dryer use.

articleSummary: Short-term exposure to major air pollutants increases influenza-like illness (ILI) risk in Shandong Province, China, based on 2015–2019 data from 16 cities, totaling 2,145,543 ILI cases. Meta-regression indicates that higher gross domestic product and denser healthcare resources mitigate these pollutant-associated risks, while basin topography exacerbates them during severe pollution episodes. Findings support localized, resource-adjusted air quality early warning systems to protect vulnerable populations from pollution-related ILI.

articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 11,000 infected and 5,400 deaths: why is it so difficult to stop Ebola in the Congo?
articleHeadline: Mais de 11 mil infetados e 5.400 mortes: porque é tão difícil travar o Ébola no Congo?
articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by the Bundibugyo variant, has killed more than 5,400 and infected over 11,000, with new cases running at 400–500 per week six months after the outbreak was declared. The epidemic has spread across 67 health zones in eight provinces. Children are disproportionately affected, accounting for more than a quarter of confirmed cases and about one third of deaths; mortality among children under five reaches roughly 70%. Late detection and weak contact tracing hamper responses. Insecurity and armed conflict impede access; the WHO notes more than 80 attacks on health facilities since the outbreak began, while population displacement and movement restrictions complicate control measures. Laboratory capacity has expanded, with about 2,000 beds available in treatment and transit facilities. The WHO stresses strengthening security and response capacity to mitigate the crisis.

articleSummary: Fiocruz reports a rise in Covid-19–related severe acute respiratory syndrome (SRAG) in six states plus the Federal District for 1–7 November, per InfoGripe, with national hospitalizations remaining low. The uptick is most evident among children and older adults, reinforcing vaccination and booster uptake. Regional increases occur in the Distrito Federal, Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná and Bahia. Among capitals, Boa Vista (RR), João Pessoa (PB), Porto Velho (RO) and Rio de Janeiro (RJ) show alert/risks, with age patterns: under-2 in Boa Vista/João Pessoa; under-4 and 50–64 in Porto Velho; and 65+ in Rio de Janeiro. In the past four epidemiological weeks, rhinovirus accounted for 49% of SRAG positives, followed by SARS-CoV-2 (11.5%), RSV (8.9%), influenza A (4.3%), and influenza B (3.9%); among deaths with viral ID, rhinovirus 43.6% and SARS-CoV-2 26.9%. articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: Warning of the risk of a continental outbreak and what is known.
articleHeadline: Ébola en la RDC: advierten riesgo de brote continental y esto se sabe
articleSummary: Ebola Virus Disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains one of the gravest in recent memory, with 11,254 confirmed cases and 5,505 deaths (case fatality 48.9%) as of 15 November 2026, spanning 67 health zones in eight provinces. The Bundibugyo strain poses additional challenges, with no vaccines or therapies as effective as those for the Zaire variant. Declared six months ago, the outbreak threatens regional and continental spread amid insecurity, population displacement, and resource shortfalls. Across the region, 80% of new cases are detected outside formal health systems, and about 65% of victims die without specialized care. Cross-border transmission has occurred: Kenya reports 9 cases and 2 deaths; Nigeria is also cited. Response includes surveillance, case isolation, and risk communication, but financing gaps (~$60 million) and security barriers impede control. The United States has imposed entry suspensions for travelers from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

articleSummary: Nov 13, 2026: Korea's Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (APQA) issued a High-Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) risk advisory as domestic poultry outbreaks rise and wild birds test positive for H5N1 and H5N9. Since Oct 12, HPAI antigens were detected in wild birds at Suncheon Bay, with a total of 10 detections to date, and six poultry-farm outbreaks: Yeoncheon and Yeoju (Gyeonggi Province) layer farms; Jangheung (Jeollanam-do) fattening duck farm; Ganghwa (Incheon) layer farm; Jincheon (Chungcheongbuk-do) breeding duck farm; and Paju (Gyeonggi) quail farm. Migratory-bird tracking shows a mallard moving south from Baicheng, Jilin, China, arriving in Uljin, North Gyeongsang, by Nov 7. In Japan, HP AI antigens were detected in wild birds/environments in Akita, Hokkaido, Kagoshima, with suspected cases in Kyoto (200,000-layer) and Chiba (40,000-layer) farms. Measures include two-stage farm-vehicle disinfection, PPE and dedicated footwear, closing back doors without anterooms, entry disinfection, hand hygiene, and intensified central inspections.

articleSummary: In Sikar district, a seasonal viral fever surge following weather changes has overwhelmed public health facilities. In the last 11 days, OPDs at CHCs and PHCs logged over 80,000 patients, about twice the normal 40–44k. Patients report high fever, joint pain, muscle aches, profound weakness, and fatigue, with gastrointestinal symptoms such as vomiting and diarrhea. Some patients show reduced platelet counts, and 36 dengue and chikungunya cases have been recorded, triggering an anti-vector response. Health authorities have initiated larval control around homes, fogging, and the deployment of MLO oil in stagnant water, while blood tests for fever patients are being intensified. Hospitals have been instructed to maintain essential medicines stock and to restrict nonessential staff leaves to ensure care. CMHO Dr. Ashok Maharia emphasized mandatory blood investigations for fever cases.

articleHeadline: Thailand's Dengue Cases and Deaths Put Prevention in Focus
articleSummary: Thailand reports 34,875 dengue infections and 47 deaths nationwide through Nov 7, 2026, with southern Health Region 11 recording transmission at 1.7 times the national average amid flood-driven mosquito breeding. Floodwaters in the Gulf of Thailand monsoon fuel late-season outbreaks; national infections peaked in August at about 1,450, versus 2,700 in August 2025. School-age children and working-age adults account for most cases, while older adults experience deadlier outcomes due to underlying conditions; officials have mobilized village health volunteers to clear larval habitats before floodwaters recede. Early dengue mimics flu; symptoms include fever 39–40 C, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, muscle aches, and nausea. Red-flag signs—vomiting, abdominal pain, skin bleeding, nosebleeds, dark stools—require emergency care. Prevention centers on eliminating standing water weekly, repairing screens, sleeping under nets, and using DEET/picaridin. Travelers should monitor weekly provincial advisories.
notes: デング熱はタイの風土病であり、今回の報告は洪水に伴う季節性の増加。2025年8月のピーク(2700件)より2026年8月のピーク(1450件)は低い。インフルエンザは症状の類似性について言及されているのみで、実際の流行ではない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control and is already the second largest in history.
articleHeadline: Surto de Ebola no Congo continua fora de controle e já é o 2° maior da história
articleSummary: As of November 15, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains out of control six months after its May 15 declaration, driven by the Bundibugyo strain. Authorities report over 11,000 cases and about 5,400 deaths, ranking it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. MSF warns surveillance gaps, weak health facilities, and difficulty identifying contacts are sustaining transmission. In Ituri, only 9% of MSF-confirmed patients had been identified as contacts beforehand. North Kivu and Haut-Uélé still lack adequate support; health centers report poor sterilization, water, chlorine, and triage. In Beni, nearly three-quarters of infections occurred in health facilities. MSF operates in five provinces with eight treatment centers and three rapid-response groups, documenting about 1,500 confirmed-patient admissions, €64.6 million spent, and roughly 2,900 staff, ~90% locally recruited.

articleHeadline: Mpox ultrapassa mil casos no Brasil e registra primeira morte em 2026 - Três Passos News
articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) infections in Brazil exceed 1,000 cases in 2026, with Rio de Janeiro recording the year's first death. A 48-year-old man with HIV-related immunosuppression died; the death was confirmed by the state health secretariat. As of Nov 12, Brazil had 1,023 confirmed cases, 46 probable, and 581 suspected, with one fatality; over half of confirmations occurred in October–November. In Rio de Janeiro, 382 confirmed cases were reported by Nov 13, with about two-thirds since Sep 13. The city accounts for roughly 70% of cases, and 55 patients were hospitalized. Mpox is caused by a virus related to smallpox and transmits mainly through close contact with infected lesions, with symptoms including fever, muscle pains, lymphadenopathy, and skin rash. Vaccination efforts include more than 2,000 doses allocated to Rio de Janeiro for priority groups, including people with HIV/AIDS; authorities urge avoidance of contact with suspected cases and prompt medical care.
notes: 死亡例はHIVによる免疫抑制患者。リオデジャネイロ州・市に症例が集中しており、ワクチン接種（2,000回分以上）が優先グループに実施されている。
